requirement_results.command: IdentityBackedAuthority satisfies the sealed AuthorityResolutionPort Protocol
RegistrationAndMarkingPolicy satisfies the sealed PolicyDecisionPort Protocol
NamedQueryGateway satisfies the sealed NamedQueryPort Protocol
a registered contract+version, an identified principal, and a resource authorized under the real marking join together reach the real TypeDB projection read and return a served response
an unregistered contract_id is denied (ARBITRARY_QUERY_FORBIDDEN) with no response of any kind ever returned
a registered contract_id at an unregistered version is denied identically to an unregistered contract, with no response
a principal never registered in the real IdentityRegistry abstains (IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS) with no response of any kind ever returned

a resource outside the requester's real marking clearance is denied with the SAME reason code as an unregistered contract (ARBITRARY_QUERY_FORBIDDEN) -- a caller cannot distinguish 'not registered' from 'marking denied' from the error alone -- and the real TypeDB projection is never reached
a resource deliberately missing its classification triple in the real Fuseki marking join is denied, never disclosed, at any clearance
a request whose classification_marking_ref has no registered clearance mapping is denied, never defaulting to permit
a registered query naming no resource parameter reaches the real TypeDB projection without a marking check, since there is nothing to authorize
a missing purpose is rejected by the sealed GovernedContext constructor before any gateway or backend call is ever made
an arbitrary, non-allow-listed contract_id shape is rejected by the sealed NamedQueryRequest constructor before any gateway or backend call is ever made

a real, lower-blast-radius network fault (a genuine closed local TCP port, the same pattern established in OCOR-DEV-0026/0027) inside the marking-authorization port propagates as a real OSError and is never silently absorbed into a PERMIT decision
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: RegistrationAndMarkingPolicy's registry and clearance_by_marking_ref are constructor-injected data, not yet backed by a live, governed registration/clearance-issuance service (that is OCOR-DEV-0048's scope, 'Integrate OPA Keycloak SPIFFE OpenBao and mTLS', a later wave-15 task this task does not depend on and does not claim to satisfy) -- this task's own scope is the smallest contract-compliant slice: the gateway's decision logic and its fail-closed composition of identity, marking and registration, not the operational provisioning of those inputs.

IdentityBackedAuthority resolves identity with IdentityRegistry.resolve()'s default confidence/margin thresholds (0.80/0.10); a caller needing different thresholds for a specific deployment must construct its own IdentityRegistry.resolve() wrapper -- out of this task's scope, since the sealed IdentityRegistry already exposes those as explicit keyword arguments.

The marking join's granularity is exactly the resource_id an incoming request's parameters happen to name; a named query returning multiple resources in one payload (list/count semantics like OCOR-DEV-0018's list_authorized/count_authorized) is not exercised here, since ProjectionReadPort.read() as sealed in OCOR-DEV-0012 returns a single NamedQueryResponse per request -- a future list-shaped named query would need its own dedicated marking-join composition, following the same pattern.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test constructs fresh IdentityRegistry/JenaMarkingProjectionAdapter/TypeDBExactCommitAdapter/NamedQueryGateway instances per test case and resets both real backends' state in fixtures; no shared mutable state persists across tests. Verified directly by 4 consecutive test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them, and by every denial test proving no response object is ever returned or leaked on any of the 4 fail-closed paths (unregistered contract, unregistered version, ambiguous identity, marking denial).
